name: Vitis

project_scope.selection_mode: B025 strict review + B144 source-status reconciliation
project_scope.note: All four have canonical records. V. cinerea and V. palmata retain scientific range HOLDs. V. cinerea var. helleri maps to V. berlandieri.

study_strategy.warning: Do not call a Central Texas Heller's grape Vitis cinerea just because an app uses a broad species concept. Flip the leaf, inspect branchlets, and keep the berlandieri/helleri taxonomic reconciliation in mind.

quick_key.if: broad heart- to kidney-shaped leaves with dense white-to-rusty wool hiding the lower surface; large dark berries
lower leaf surface remains visible, sparsely webby/hairy to nearly glabrous; branchlets slightly angled; ripe berries conspicuously glaucous in short compact clusters
quick_key.then: Vitis berlandieri — canonical PASS; includes source-name V. cinerea var. helleri

quick_key.if: strict cinerea concept with angled branchlets densely short-hairy plus cobwebby; lower leaf remains visibly gray/green; small slightly glaucous berries
uniformly red/purplish-red/chestnut branchlets and usually deeply 3–5-lobed leaves with long-pointed lobes; lower surface essentially glabrous

curation_status.visual_status: field-ready provisional gallery: 4 canonical species, 12 physical licensed image files, 9 linked photo panels, microscopy & range HOLDs preserved

comparison_matrix.cinerea: Blade visible, gray-green, short-hairy and webby

look_here_first: Find a tendril opposite a leaf. Flip a mature leaf to inspect underside hair density, then compare current-year branchlets and intact ripe berries.
diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched mature leaf underside macros of all four species
Same-age branchlet macros showing hair architecture
Intact berry clusters with ruler and undisturbed wax bloom
Matched whole leaves documenting lobing variation
overlap_cautions: Mustang grape can develop deeply lobed leaves on vigorous shoots.
Berry wax can rub off; avoid identification from bloom alone.
V. cinerea and V. palmata are canonical but remain range HOLDs.
Source-name V. cinerea var. helleri is represented by V. berlandieri.
shared_genus_pattern: Woody vines with alternate simple leaves, leaf-opposed tendrils/inflorescences, small flowers and fleshy grape berries. At the node, a tendril opposite the leaf is the fastest genus cue.

realistic_lookalikes.difference: Three separate leaflets, not one simple Vitis blade; inspect leaflet joints.
Usually five distinct palmately arranged leaflets; Vitis has a simple leaf.
Tendrils arise from leaf axils, not opposite leaves; corona-bearing flowers.

targeted_handoff.request: Verify quantitative branchlet pubescence and berry/cluster characters distinguishing strict V. cinerea from V. berlandieri. Preserve the source-concept mapping of V. cinerea var. helleri to V. berlandieri and existing range HOLDs.

media_guidance: Existing V. berlandieri leaf-face and V. mustangensis fruit-face images may anchor overview cards. They do not substitute for matched diagnostic underside, branchlet, and fruit macros; Diagnostic Photo Polish owns photo acquisition.

visual_comparison.title: Texas grapevine identification — flip the leaf before trusting the fruit
visual_comparison.subtitle: Physical licensed photos arranged around leaf underside, branching habit and confusers. Species HOLD decisions preserved.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHITE FELT = Mustang. Visible underside + glaucous compact berries = Berlandier/Heller. Short-hairy webby angled stems = strict cinerea (HOLD). Red branchlets + deeply lobed leaves = palmata (HOLD). THREE leaflets/three-parted foliage = sorrelvine, Cissus.
look_here_first_sequence: Check whether a grape-family tendril arises opposite a leaf (rather than from the leaf axil as in Passiflora).
Count separate leaflets: Vitis has one simple leaf, Cissus trifoliata usually has three leaflets but can have a single 3-lobed blade.
Flip a mature leaf: white felt hiding the underside in Mustang versus leaf tissue visible in Berlandier/Heller.
Inspect stems at the newest nodes: red/purple in palmata, angled/hairy in strict cinerea, slight webby in berlandieri.
If present, compare intact ripening clusters and wax bloom after leaf/stem characters, never first.

items.label: 1. Mustang grape — canopy-scale climber
items.caption: Recognize the big woody climber in Honey Creek State Natural Area, Comal County. For identification, move from this big picture to an actual leaf underside.
items.creator: Larry D. Moore

items.label: 2. Mustang — individual leaf appearance
items.caption: The blade remains ONE SIMPLE LEAF even if lobed. Flip it to find Mustang's characteristic opaque whitish wool beneath; this particular image is not certified as a hair macro.
items.creator: sonnia hill

items.label: 3. Berlandier's grape — underside
items.image_role: Underside leaf photograph, central comparison character
items.caption: Contrast this visibly surfaced leaf underside with Mustang's dense opaque white felt. The specimen was photographed in French cultivation; its photo cannot prove Texas county presence.
items.creator: Pancrat

items.label: 4. Berlandier's grape — Texas view
items.image_role: Texas exact-species recognition and general foliage
items.caption: Teach the Berlandier's/Heller's taxon concept. Some resources still call this V. cinerea var. helleri; Kew treats it as V. berlandieri.
items.creator: Joachim Schmid

items.label: 5. True graybark grape — leaf reference
items.caption: Recognize the graybark grape leaf concept; branchlet short hairs and small fruit remain decisive. This source concept stays taxonomy/range HOLD in the private learner.
items.creator: Robert H. Mohlenbrock / USDA-NRCS

items.label: 6. Graybark grape — botanical garden comparison
items.image_role: Cultivated specimen supporting leaf appearance only
items.caption: Cultivated Berlin specimen gives a second foliage angle; it cannot resolve historic Texas V. cinerea versus V. berlandieri naming or county nativity.
items.creator: BotBln

items.label: 7. Catbird grape — USDA leaf
items.caption: Look for 3–5 pointed lobes, then independently verify the distinctly red/purple young branchlets and relatively hairless underside. Leaf lobing overlaps other grapes; county range HOLD remains.
items.creator: Robert H. Mohlenbrock / USDA-NRCS

items.label: 8. Catbird grape — second USDA view
items.caption: Additional species reference; no reliably calibrated photo of red branchlet or glabrous undersurface is installed, so keep those on the final-polish request list.
items.creator: Robert H. Mohlenbrock / USDA-NRCS

items.label: 9. Sorrelvine: do not confuse with grape
items.caption: Cissus usually shows THREE leaflets, sometimes a single three-lobed leaf; Vitis typically has one continuous simple blade. Examine leaflet joints and tendrils.
items.creator: DouglasGoldman

field_cautions: Vitis cinerea and V. palmata remain scientific range HOLDs, though approved for the private learner.
Vitis cinerea var. helleri is an alias of canonical Vitis berlandieri under Kew; do not duplicate under cinerea.
Mustang can have deeply 3–5-lobed growth leaves; lobing alone is not decisive.
Some images are from cultivation or outside Central Texas: they teach morphology, NOT native county evidence.
Do not place arrows on precise hair/nodes unless coordinates visually reviewed on the installed JPEG.
